title: Salmon Ladder, Phase 14 (paper v17): the cross-fitted ladder - a read-out that is itself a conformal p-value - with its seed rule, level and static-rank combination selected on the development splits before any test-set run; transductive baselines; backbone families; other base detectors; the OpenOOD CIFAR-100 benchmark
status: Registered before any Phase 14 computation on the development splits or on the test sets (the code is written and smoke-tested on synthetic data only). The selection rule below is implemented verbatim in sel14.py (aggregate) and is applied mechanically; the test-set scripts read the chosen configuration from its output.
motivation: Reviews of v16: (1) the seeds add 1-2 FPR95 points on top of p+, (2) the guarantee (Proposition 3) covers the seed selection, not the final score, (3) r <= 5 is lost to the static rank and Storey saturates at high mixing rates, (4) no transductive / graph-based baseline on the same features, (5) the configuration history is post hoc, (6) ImageNet-1K-family benchmarks and DINO backbones only.

method.graph: unchanged: k-NN graph (k_g = 10) over support + calibration + test images per view, W = max(A, A^T), S = D^-1/2 W D^-1/2, lambda = 0.9, propagation to the fixed point; views DINOv2 L/14 + DINOv3 L/16 (Phase 12 selection); 12 support + 4 calibration images per class
method.cross_fit: the calibration images and the test images are split at random into two folds (rng seed [14, 0]; folds = parity of the arrival index in the arrival-time mode). In fold b the seeds are selected by BH on the calibrated ranks p+ of the fold's test images against the fold's own calibration images (Proposition 3 applies per fold); the mass u- of the seeds is propagated. A node of fold b' (calibration or test image) is scored by s = sum over views of [log p+ (rank of u+ among the OTHER fold's calibration images) + log p- (rank of u- of the OTHER fold's seeds among the other fold's calibration images) (+ log p_static, or min with it, by mode)]; p_final = rank of s among the OWN fold's calibration images (1 + #{cal <= s}) / (n_cal_fold + 1).
method.claim_to_prove: Proposition 4 (to be stated in v17): for every fold, if the fold's calibration images and its ID test images are exchangeable, p_final of each ID test image is super-uniform (P(p_final <= alpha) <= alpha) and the p_final of the fold's test images are PRDS on the ID ones, hence BH on p_final within a fold controls the FDR of the final selection at the nominal level, and the rule p_final <= alpha has ID false-alarm rate <= alpha. Proof: s is a function of the node features that is invariant to permutations of the fold's calibration + test images (the graph, u+, the other fold's seeds and u-, and the other fold's calibration reference do not depend on which of them is called calibration), so condition (8) of Marandon et al. 2024 (AdaDetect, Theorem 3.3 / Corollary 3.5) holds with the fold's calibration images as the null sample; Benjamini-Yekutieli 2001 for BH under PRDS.
method.candidates_18: rule in {storey (Storey-AdaDetect level, Cor. 3.7, lambda_S = floor(n/2)/(n+1) with n = the fold's calibration size), bh (plain BH level)} x q in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2} x mode in {pp (p+ p-), pps (p+ p- x static), min (min of log p+ p- and log p_static)}; p_static = prototype-cosine rank (nearest class prototype = mean of the 12 support features), read in the same cross-fitted way
method.references_scored_alongside: p+ only (cross-fitted), static alone (cross-fitted), the Phase 12 read-out v1 (asymmetric seeds, Storey, q in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2}), kNN rank (k = 10), LGC-max (transductive label propagation of the support class labels on the same graph, max class mass read as a calibrated rank), each standalone and x base
method.fold_pooled_statistic: the fold-pooled s is recorded as a diagnostic (|pooled rows) but is not a candidate: the method's output is p_final

selection_rule.data: development splits dev1 (selection) and dev2 (confirmation) of Phase 5 (R5 caches: 5 draws x {near, far} x 3 orders each), the same splits used in Phase 12; no test image
selection_rule.rule: min dev1 near FPR95 over the 18 cross-fit candidates (rule x q x mode; views L14+D3L; standalone) subject to dev1 far FPR95 <= that of the Phase 12 read-out (v1|storey|q0.2|pp, standalone) + 0.5; dev2 reported as confirmation only
selection_rule.unit: draw (the three orders of a draw averaged first), as in Phase 12
selection_rule.ties: to 0.01 FPR95 points: lower far FPR95, then the simpler read-out (pp before pps before min), Storey before BH, larger q
selection_rule.fallback: if no candidate is feasible, the candidate with the smallest dev1 far FPR95 is chosen and the paper says so
selection_rule.what_is_then_fixed: the chosen (rule, q, mode) is used unchanged on every test set, benchmark and backbone below; the two fixed references (storey q = 0.2, bh q = 0.2) are always reported next to it

test_set_analyses.benchmarks: OpenOOD v1.5 ImageNet-1K near / far and Four-OOD, benchmark calibration (4 training images per class), six draws of the labelled images (p3 + Phase 4 pool draws 0-4), standalone and x TINS (per stream order), x TANL / NegLabel / AdaNeg (Phase 10 official scores) where available; means over draws, 95% t intervals over draws; paired intervals vs v1 (same base), vs p+ only (same base), vs standalone
test_set_analyses.validity: exchangeable calibration (4 ID validation images per class, three splits as Phase 13): realised P(p_final <= alpha) of the ID test images for alpha in {0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2}, realised FDP and recall of BH on p_final per fold at q (the chosen q and 0.2); also recorded under benchmark calibration
test_set_analyses.grid: the Phase 12/13 recurrence x mixing-rate grid (same test sets): the chosen configuration, the two references, p+ only, static, v1; the question is whether the chosen read-out stays at or below the static rank for r <= 5 (where v1 lost) and whether seeds saturate at the highest mixing rates
test_set_analyses.imagenet200: OpenOOD ImageNet-200 (six draws, standalone) with all 18 candidates recorded (descriptive; the chosen configuration is the one reported in the main text)
test_set_analyses.backbones: OpenOOD ImageNet-1K, the p3 draw, every single view available (DINOv2 B/14, L/14, DINOv3 B/16, L/16, CLIP ViT-B/16 image embedding, DINO v1 ViT-B/16): chosen configuration vs v1 vs p+ only vs kNN vs LGC-max, standalone and x TINS
test_set_analyses.cifar100: OpenOOD v1.5 CIFAR-100 (near: CIFAR-10, TIN; far: MNIST, SVHN, Textures, Places365), the same frozen features (DINOv2 L/14, DINOv3 L/16 on the 32 x 32 images resized as any other image), six disjoint draws of 16 training images per class (rng [14, 100]), standalone; compared with the published OpenOOD v1.5 numbers (trained methods) and with the same-feature baselines; validity of p_final
test_set_analyses.online: arrival-time mode of the cross-fit (folds = arrival parity; chosen rule and q; pp, pps, min emitted), the same stream files as Phase 13, standalone and x TINS; validity of p_final; iteration counts and seconds per stream

hypotheses.H1: the chosen cross-fitted read-out is within 1 FPR95 point of v1 on dev2 near (the price of validity is small)
hypotheses.H2: under exchangeable calibration, P(p_final <= 0.05) is in [0.04, 0.06] on every data set and the realised FDP of BH on p_final is at most q + 0.02 on every data set (the guarantee holds in practice)
hypotheses.H3: the chosen read-out is at most 2 FPR95 points worse than the static rank at r <= 5 on the grid and better than v1 at r >= 10 or within 1 point of it
hypotheses.H4: plain BH seeds do not saturate at the highest mixing rates (ID fraction among seeds <= q m0 / m), while Storey seeds do when pi0_hat < q
hypotheses.H5: on CIFAR-100 the standalone read-out reaches the near-OOD AUROC of the best published OpenOOD v1.5 trained method within 2 points

disclosure: The configurations of Phases 10-13 (views, q = 0.2, the product with the static rank, DINOv3) were chosen with the OpenOOD test sets in view (disclosed in v14-v16). Phase 14 adds nothing chosen on a test set: the cross-fit design, the candidate set and the selection rule are fixed here; the dev splits are the Phase 5 development data.
deviations: recorded in prereg_p14_amendments.json and in the paper
